new_docs.claims_summary: YipitData's licensed spend panel estimates 1Q26 AWS revenue growth of 29.3% y/y (above Visible Alpha consensus of 25.4%, incl. Trainium/OpenAI and Bedrock-scaling adjustments), Azure F3Q26 growth of 38.6% (slightly below its 40% consensus, EMEA weakest), and Google Cloud 1Q26 growth of 53.1% (above its 50.2% consensus). It also shows AWS's share of combined AI tokens rising to 51% in Mar-26 from 16% a year earlier, while Azure's fell from 53% to 27%, and flags very-early (low-confidence) Q2-to-date reads for AWS/Azure through early April.

entry_orbs.why: revenue-drivers' own WHAT-TO-READ list names 'a measured panel's read on a driver (segment growth...)' as a source; this panel is exactly that for AWS/cloud revenue growth and the AI-workload driver, at a materiality the module's Q1 2026 read (28% YoY from the 10-Q) does not yet capture at this granularity (AI token share, GPU/Graviton mix).

guidance-consensus' WHAT-TO-READ explicitly names 'External alt-data panels... a measured panel's estimate of the same metric, with its vendor error margin; cross-check only, never the consensus source' — this panel gives an independent VA-consensus comparison (AWS/Azure/GCP estimate vs consensus, with stated 2.3/4/6pp margins of error) that the current run's consensus read does not carry.

The AI-token-share swing (AWS 51% vs Azure 27%, from 16%/53% a year prior) is competitive-economics evidence bearing directly on the moat verdict's AWS-vs-Azure-vs-GCP competitive-position read, though the agent's own WHAT-TO-READ list does not name alt-data panels explicitly, hence the lower confidence.

new_docs.claims_summary: CEO Andy Jassy reportedly said Amazon's custom-chip business already has $225B in commitments and has topped a $20B annual revenue run rate, growing at triple-digit rates y/y.

entry_orbs.why: If true, a disclosed $225B chip-commitment figure and $20B run-rate would be a new, material revenue driver beyond AWS cloud consumption; but this is a single tier-10 wire report of a CEO quote with no filing or second independent source in the pool confirming the figures, so per INTAKE.md §5 it defaults to note_only rather than driving a rerun.

summary: Five documents landed since the 2026-07-10 run finished: one tier-5 YipitData cloud-spend panel (Mar-26 update) and four tier-10 screener wire events. The YipitData panel clears the materiality gate (68) — it gives an independent VA-consensus cross-check on AWS/Azure/GCP 1Q26 growth and shows AWS's AI-token share extending its lead over Azure, bearing on earnings/revenue-drivers, earnings/guidance-consensus, and business-model/moat. Scope the rerun to those three orbs and their cascade. All four wire events (chip-commitment quote, a generic capex-comparison piece, a routine Florida facility closure, and a speculative external-chip-sales story) are single tier-10 sources with no filing or second independent source backing them, so per INTAKE.md §5 they stay note_only — most notably the $225B chip-commitment claim, which would be material if corroborated but is not yet.
